name: infra_deepspeed
title: DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 trainer driven by ds_config.json
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the config-driven trainer the ROADMAP's framework list names
note: A precision trap for the absence rules. The documented DeepSpeed step is engine.backward(loss) / engine.step(), and engine.step() zeroes the gradients itself, so the absence of optimizer.zero_grad() here is correct. The batch size, learning rate, optimizer, scheduler and precision are all in ds_config.json rather than in Python, which is what a config-driven trainer looks like to a static reader.
stagesObserved: config, data, model, objective, train, eval present; `deliver` is reported absent although engine.save_checkpoint(args.save_dir, ...) writes the checkpoint at line 104 - see the domain-infra report, finding INFRA-04.

forbidden.why: the training loader is not constructed here at all: deepspeed.initialize(training_data=train_set) returns it, and DeepSpeed builds it with its own distributed sampler
the validation sampler is constructed with shuffle=False at line 87 and the loader passes no shuffle=
num_workers=2 is passed at line 89 but the module ends in `if __name__ == "__main__": main()` at line 107 and the loader is built inside main()
the DeepSpeed engine zeroes the gradients inside engine.step() (line 99); calling optimizer.zero_grad() by hand in a DeepSpeed loop is the mistake, not the fix
engine.step() at line 99 is the optimizer step; DeepSpeed owns the optimizer that deepspeed.initialize returned
engine.backward(loss) at line 98 precedes engine.step() at line 99
evaluate() accumulates criterion(...).item(), a Python float, and the training loop accumulates nothing
evaluate() calls engine.eval() at line 48 and restores engine.train() at line 58
the evaluation loop is inside `with torch.no_grad():` at line 51
both loops move features and labels to engine.device before the forward pass
there is no .cuda() and no 'cuda' literal in this file; the device comes from engine.device
torch.manual_seed(7) is called at line 39, before any tensor is drawn
CaptionScorer.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 11
the checkpoint goes through engine.save_checkpoint, not torch.save of a module, and this file never calls torch.load
